subject: Next steps: NovaRetail trial — sprint map & deliverables
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@novaretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps: NovaRetail trial — sprint map & deliverables

Hi Marta — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick summary and proposed plan so we have a single source of truth: 

Recap (from discovery)
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for NovaRetail search & recommendations pipeline for holiday peak (decimated test traffic).
- Primary stakeholders: Marta (product), Sam (platform/infra), Procurement (contract).

Proposed POC success criteria (draft)
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 200 ms for 512-token requests under baseline load (see evaluation plan).
- Concurrency: sustain 100 concurrent inference requests with P95 < 300 ms (you asked for this during the call).
- Quality: recommendation relevance measured by click-through delta >= +6% vs baseline on the sample prompt set.
- Integration: successful end-to-end call from your staging service to Redwood endpoints with KV caching enabled.
- Security: customer data never leaves NovaRetail VPC; audit logs available for the trial.

Evaluation plan (how we'll measure)
- We will run a controlled workload using your anonymized sample traces and our synthetic spike tests.
- Weekly readouts will include token-level cost, p95 latency, error rate, and qualitative RL feedback from your product team.

Timeline (proposal)
- Week 0 (Dec 6): Kickoff + environment access + procurement paperwork kickoff.
- Week 1 (Dec 7–13): Integration + test traffic ingestion (owner: Sam).
- Week 2 (Dec 14–20): Load tests, stability, and quality evaluation (owner: Redwood engs).
- Week 3 (Dec 21–23): Final readout, decision meeting, and next-step proposal.

Weekly check-ins: Tuesdays 10:00am PT (proposed) — 30 min.

Owner map
- Redwood: Diego (trial lead), Laura (deployment/runbook), Karthik (performance tuning).
- NovaRetail: Marta (product owner), Sam (infra owner), Procurement contact for contract/PO.

Attachments: trial-scope.xlsx, sample-eval-prompts.md (attached for your review).

Ask for this email: please confirm the success criteria above and whether Dec 6 kickoff works for you (we can shift by a day if needed). Also, please add the procurement contact so we can start any contract/PO steps in parallel.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

--
Diego Fernandez
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.ai

From: Marta Ruiz <marta@novaretail.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Green <sam.green@novaretail.com>, procurement@novaretail.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: NovaRetail trial — sprint map & deliverables

Diego — thanks for the thorough write-up, this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Concurrency target: yes, 100 concurrent requests is what we want to validate; if you can show a P95 < 300ms at that level we're happy (we understand the 200ms target at baseline loads).
2) Security: we require that the audit logs cover request IDs and token counts — can you confirm Redwood will provide those for the trial?
3) Timeline: Dec 6 for kickoff is good, but our lead infra (Sam) is on leave Dec 8–9, so if we need deep troubleshooting it may push a task to week 2.

Procurement: looping in procurement (procurement@novaretail.com) — they will need a short SOW and an estimated spend range to open the PO request.

Can you also add a short runbook that lists the exact endpoints we will call and the keys/roles needed? If you can send that before kickoff we will use it to provision an integration account.

Thanks — Marta

--
Marta Ruiz
Head of Product, NovaRetail
marta@novaretail.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@novaretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@novaretail.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps: NovaRetail trial — sprint map & deliverables

Thanks Marta — quick replies inline: 

> Concurrency target: yes, 100 concurrent requests...
We will validate both baselines (single-session steady-state) and scaled concurrency. We'll show p95s for both.

> Security / audit logs
Yes — we will deliver request-level audit logs for the trial that include request IDs, token counts, timestamps, and model variant. I will attach a short runbook prior to kickoff with the endpoints and required IAM roles.

> Timeline and Sam's availability
Understood. We can keep Dec 6 kickoff as a soft start: Day 0 will be access + runbook review, then move to integration when Sam is available. If major infra work is blocked we will shift some of the load tests into Week 2 and keep progress on QA, eval prompt runs, and cost estimates.

I'll loop internally to lock owners and the runbook.

On Fri, Nov 27, 2026 at 09:22 AM Marta Ruiz <marta@novaretail.com> wrote:
> Diego — thanks for the thorough write-up...

Diego
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@novaretail.com>, Sam Green <sam.green@novaretail.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:48:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Next steps: NovaRetail trial — sprint map & deliverables

Diego/Karthik — attaching the POC runbook and an updated sprint map with owners and gating criteria. I added more operational detail so NovaRetail can provision access before kickoff.

NR-POC-runbook-v1.pdf (attached) — includes:
- Exact endpoint URIs and header examples (staging + fallback endpoints)
- Required roles and token scope for a staging integration key
- How to enable KV prefix caching and expected metrics to collect
- Rollback steps if we see elevated error rates during load tests

Updated sprint map (high level):
- Dec 6: Kickoff, account access, runbook review (Owners: Diego, Marta, Sam)
- Dec 7–10: Integration and small-scale smoke tests (Owners: Sam (infra), Laura (eng support))
- Dec 13–17: Performance tuning and concurrency testing (Owners: Karthik, Redwood-Perf)
- Dec 20–22: Final readout and decision (Owners: Diego, Marta)

Go/no-go gating (proposed):
- Functional integration passes (end-to-end calls succeed)
- Error rate < 0.5% during sustained 30-min load at target concurrency
- Quality: sample prompts show at least break-even or better CTR vs baseline in our hand-eval set

Drive link to materials: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1N_Retail-POC

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
